label: Northstar Bike Co.: three transactions
text: Alex invests $5,000 cash to start the business (assets +$5,000 cash, equity +$5,000 capital); buys a $1,200 bike repair stand on credit (assets +$1,200 equipment, liabilities +$1,200 payable); earns $300 cash from bike sales (assets +$300 cash, equity +$300 revenue).

label: Journal entry: repair stand bought for cash
text: Northstar Bike Co. pays $1,200 cash to buy a new repair stand: debit Equipment (Asset) $1,200, credit Cash (Asset) $1,200. Total debits ($1,200) = total credits ($1,200).

label: Northstar's balance sheet
text: As of December 31, 2025: Cash $8,500, Accounts Receivable $1,200, Inventory $2,300, Repair & Shop Equipment $14,000 less Accumulated Depreciation ($2,000); Total Assets $24,000. Accounts Payable $1,800, Bank Loan (long-term) $6,200, Owner's Capital $14,000, Retained Earnings $2,000; Total Liabilities + Equity $24,000. Balance check: Assets $24,000 = Liabilities $8,000 + Equity $16,000.

label: Northstar's income statement
text: Year Ended December 31, 2025: Sales Revenue $52,000 less Cost of Goods Sold ($21,000) = Gross Profit $31,000; operating expenses Wages ($14,000), Rent ($6,000), Depreciation ($2,000), Utilities & Other ($1,500); Operating Income $7,500; less Interest Expense ($500); Net Income $7,000.

label: Northstar's cash flow statement
text: Year Ended December 31, 2025. Operating: Net Income $7,000 + Depreciation (non-cash) $2,000 + Decrease in Inventory $500 less Increase in Receivables ($300) = Net Cash from Operations $9,200. Investing: Purchase of Equipment ($3,000). Financing: Owner Contribution $1,000, Loan Repayment ($1,200), net ($200). Net Change in Cash: $9,200 - $3,000 - $200 = +$6,000.

label: The custom bike build
text: Northstar Bike Co. completes a custom bike build on December 28, 2025 and invoices the client $2,000; the client pays on January 15, 2026. Cash basis records the revenue in January 2026 (when paid); accrual basis records it in December 2025 (when earned).

label: Northstar's delivery van
text: Delivery van: cost $32,000, salvage value $2,000, useful life 5 years. ($32,000 - $2,000) ÷ 5 = $6,000 per year. Book value falls from $26,000 at the end of year 1 to $2,000 at the end of year 5.

label: Northstar's ratios in action
text: Current Ratio: $12,000 ÷ $8,000 = 1.5. Debt-to-Equity: $8,000 ÷ $16,000 = 0.5. A current ratio above 1.0 and modest debt-to-equity both signal a financially healthy bike shop. A chart beside them shows two bars, 59.6 and 13.5.

label: Strong net income, low cash
text: Discussion question: Northstar Bike Co. has strong net income but low cash on hand. How is that possible, and which statement would you check first to find out?
